provenance.note: Fitted to the operator’s DMC2 Mini test log, not a specification. 24,000 RPM and the 10,000 mm/min feed ceiling are Shariff’s published figures. The 6,000 RPM floor admits the manufacturer-chart rows down to 6,600 RPM; the slowest tested speed was 10,000 RPM and low-speed spindle cooling is not modelled. The 950 W / 0.378 N·m plateau is not the 2.2 kW nameplate: it is the effective constant-torque output under Cutspace’s constant-coefficient force model, chosen so the aggressive test cuts sit at or below usable output (3 mm aluminium at 22,000 RPM and 4 mm steel at 16,000 RPM reach about 92–95%) and the recorded high-feed spindle bog-downs at 24,000 RPM sit beyond it. It folds in thin-chip force effects and whatever the spindle really delivers. Deep, thin-radial stalls with 10–12 mm tools are not power events in this model; the per-tool deflection allowances in the recipes capture those.

recipes.name: Mild steel · 8 mm · slot 0.25D deep (chart)
recipes.notes: “Pre-hardened steel 40–50 HRC” column of the 4-flute coated chart: 12,000 RPM, 770 mm/min, 8 mm stepover (100%D) × 2 mm depth (25%D), 0.0160 mm/tooth. Outside the fitted DMC2 envelope: tool deflection 138%, spindle torque 130%. The tests never ran this tool this heavily; the heaviest success was steel profile at 18,000 RPM, 1,100 mm/min, 0.03 mm stepover × 24 mm depth. Treat the chart row as unsupported on this machine rather than as a starting point.
